questions.q: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit and Motion Path are categories of:
questions.solution: These four are animation effect types acting on objects within a slide. Transitions only control slide-to-slide changeover.
questions.shortcut: Object effects = animation (the 4 categories listed); slide changeover = transition.

questions.q: In MS Excel, the shortcut Shift+F3 opens the:
questions.solution: In Excel, Shift+F3 opens Insert Function (the fx dialog). The change-case meaning belongs to MS Word, which is the trap. Name Manager is Ctrl+F3.
questions.shortcut: Same key, different app: Word = case, Excel = function.

questions.q: Which of the following is regarded as the first commercially available computer?
questions.solution: UNIVAC-I (1951) was the first computer produced and sold commercially. ENIAC was a one-off military project; EDVAC was a stored-program research machine; IBM 360 is a 3rd-generation family (1964).
questions.shortcut: UNIVAC = the first computer you could BUY; ENIAC = the first one ever BUILT electronically.

questions.q: The correct sequence of steps in a single machine cycle is:
questions.solution: The CPU first Fetches the instruction from memory, Decodes it in the control unit, Executes it in the ALU, and Stores the result.
questions.shortcut: Fat Dogs Eat Snacks: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store. Any option starting with Decode/Execute is out.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

Government by the people through their elected representatives
questions.solution: Demos = people + cracy = rule → **democracy**. The stem names the ruler ('the people'); the other options name one ruler, officials, and nobles respectively.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** The Internet has changed education forever. **P:** Students in remote villages now attend world-class lectures. **Q:** Quality no longer depends on location. **R:** However, screen fatigue is a real cost. **S:** Teachers must blend online lessons with offline care. **6.** The classroom of the future will be hybrid.
questions.solution: **P** (village access) → **Q** (the principle it proves) → **R** ('However' cost) → **S** (the blending remedy) → S6 (hybrid future). PQRS.
questions.shortcut: However-clause follows the gains; remedy sentence precedes S6.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A medicine that counteracts the effects of poison
questions.solution: Counteracts poison = **antidote**. *Antibiotic* attacks bacteria, *antiseptic* prevents wound infection, *anaesthetic* kills sensation during surgery.
questions.shortcut: anti- family; function match: poison → antidote.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

At the drop of a hat
questions.solution: A dropped hat was the instant signal to begin a fight or race → **immediately, without needing any reason**. 'Reluctance' and 'planning' contradict the idiom's whole point.
questions.shortcut: Signal picture: hat drops, action starts.

questions.q: Which river is known to cross the Tropic of Cancer twice?
questions.solution: The **Mahi** rises in the Vindhyas of Madhya Pradesh, flows north into Rajasthan, turns back south-west through Gujarat and enters the **Gulf of Khambhat** — crossing the **Tropic of Cancer twice**.

questions.q: With which neighbouring country does India share its longest international land border?
questions.solution: India's border with **Bangladesh** is about **4,096.7 km** — the longest. China (3,488 km) and Pakistan (3,323 km) follow. The shortest is with Afghanistan (106 km).
questions.shortcut: 'Big Cats Prowl Near My Big Area' — B first.

questions.q: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.solution: The **liver** is the largest gland (and largest internal organ). It secretes bile, stores glycogen and detoxifies substances. The pituitary is the 'master gland', not the largest.

questions.q: **Garba**, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023, is a dance form of —
questions.solution: **Garba of Gujarat** is performed around a lamp (*garbo*) during Navratri. It became India's 15th ICH element in December 2023.

questions.q: The range of the data 14, 7, 22, 9, 31, 18 is:
A speed of 54 km/h expressed in m/s is:
Six years ago the ratio of the ages of A and B was 5 : 6. Six years hence this ratio will become 6 : 7. B's present age is:
questions.solution:
Ages 6 years ago: 5x, 6x. Six years hence: $5x + 12$, $6x + 12$.
$\frac{5x + 12}{6x + 12} = \frac{6}{7}$ ⇒ $35x + 84 = 36x + 72$ ⇒ $x = 12$.
B now $= 6 \times 12 + 6 = 78$ years.
questions.shortcut: The 12-year gap between the two time points adds 12 to each age. Solve 7(5x+12) = 6(6x+12) ⇒ x = 12 ⇒ B = 78.

questions.q: An article costing ₹1,000 is marked 25% above cost and then sold at a 15% discount. The profit earned is:
Pointing to a man in a photograph, Priya said, **"He is the father of my brother's niece."** How is the man related to Priya?
questions.solution: Priya's brother's niece = a daughter of Priya or of another sibling. Priya is the brother's only sister, so the niece is Priya's own daughter — and her father is Priya's **husband**.
questions.shortcut: 'My brother's niece' = your own daughter (when you are the only sister). Her father = your husband.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Sales of mobile phones in the city rose sharply during the festival month of October this year.

**Conclusions:**
I. Every year, people in the city buy more phones in festival months than in other months.
II. Mobile phone prices were reduced in October.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: I stretches one year's data to 'every year' — overgeneralisation, **does not follow**. II supplies a cause (price cut) the statement never mentions — outside information, **does not follow**. Answer: **Neither**.
questions.shortcut: One observation ≠ a rule; an unstated cause ≠ a conclusion.

questions.q: In a certain code, **CANDLE** is written as **ACDNEL**. Which word is written as **ISVLRE** in that code?
questions.solution: CANDLE → CA | ND | LE → AC | DN | EL: pairs swapped. Swapping pairs again undoes the code: IS | VL | RE → SI | LV | ER → **SILVER**.
questions.shortcut: A pair swap is its own reverse — apply the same swap to the code to get the word.
